content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: tempest-family request rate spike detected across us-west-2 and eu-west-1. 95th latency > 2s, error rate up 3%. auto-sculpt kicked in for a subset of tenants. paging oncall group. thread created 1967004322

maria: seeing the same in the console, requests/sec to tempest-14/17 have tripled over 10m. tailing logs show bursts of function_call behavior from a single partner org.

sam: can we confirm whether this is synthetic traffic or actual customer load? I see a few high-volume API keys with elevated tokens.

li: quick triage: traffic breakdown by model_family shows 78% of surge on "tempest" variants; fallback models (breeze, zephyr) look normal. root cause unknown.

maria: @sam @li I'm going to start live mitigation: reduce TPM for tempest-family from 150 -> 45 and RPM from 900 -> 300 for public tier, keep enterprise carveouts. Will post commands and runbook refs.

opsbot: Command queued: apply-rate-sculpt --family tempest --tpm 45 --rpm 300 --scope public --dry-run false

sam: :thumbsup: do we want to disable function calling for tempest while we sculpt? that reduces token churn massively.

maria: yes, good call. toggling function_calling=false in routing policy for tempest. This will be global for public customers.

jamal: notifying CS and trust: @support-bot can you open a CS alert for affected orgs and add the temporary mitigation note?

support-bot: CS Alert created: tickets queued for top 12 orgs by usage. Message template: "We've applied temporary rate limits to reduce latency; no data loss expected. Reach out if you see degradation."

li: applied the rate-sculpt. Observability: token throughput dropped ~62% for tempest family in 45s, 95th latency improving. Errors still slightly elevated for some tenants.

maria: for audit and rollback: runbook link: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/live-mitigation
Commands used: 
```
# reduce TPM/RPM for tempest public
redwoodctl shard apply-rate-sculpt --selector family=tempest --tpm=45 --rpm=300 --scope=public --note "emergency sculpt 1967004322"
# disable function calling
redwoodctl route update --family=tempest --set feature.function_calling=false --note "disable functions during sculpt"
```

li: re-route plan: set smart-routing fallback to breeze-family for non-enterprise tenants above 95th latency. This is non-destructive and per-request. Will update routing config in 2m.

opsbot: Routing update queued: set-fallback --from-family=tempest --to-family=breeze --threshold-95p-latency=1200ms --scope=public

maria: @taylor can you watch infra GPU queuing? I want to ensure we're not hitting backend queuing that causes head-of-line latency.

taylor: on it. checking GPU utilization and queue depth... queues look slightly elevated on nodes serving tempest-14 but within limits. No restart needed yet.

jamal: support ping: a large partner (org-id: 8421) reports slowed requests. I flagged them for enterprise carveout - they should be exempt. @maria confirm?

maria: confirmed. enterprise keys exempted. I added explicit override for org 8421. Command: 
```
redwoodctl quota override --org 8421 --family tempest --tpm 250 --rpm 1500 --duration 2h --note "enterprise carveout during surge"
```

li: telemetry update 1967004500: latency 95p dropped from 2100ms -> 980ms after sculpt and function toggle. Errors down to 0.9% from 3.1%. Good impact.

sam: nice. what's next for mitigation? we should throttle new sessions from suspicious API keys and request internal security to investigate synthetic traffic.

maria: @cecilia please escalate to sec-team with the top 8 API keys (I've exported keys to /tmp/surge-keys-1967004322.csv). Also enable short-lived token challenge for those keys (rate-limit + challenge)

cecilia: on it. Sec team alerted and will take over investigation. Adding rate-limit-challenge rule: 
```
redwoodctl security rate-challenge add --keys-file /tmp/surge-keys-1967004322.csv --challenge-type captcha --ttl 30m
```

opsbot: telemetry snapshot saved to s3://rb-infra/alerts/1967004322/snapshot.json

maria: preparing handoff to night oncall in 30m. I'll leave mitigation in place unless SLOs stabilize further. Handoff checklist: current sculpt config, enterprise carveouts, keys under challenge, runbook link, CS tickets created.

jamal: adding note for night: monitor breeze fallback latency and check for regression in quality alerts (because fallback -> model change may affect output).

li: followup item: schedule post-mortem if root cause is external abuse; if it's a legitimate sudden popularity spike, we'll need capacity plan. Tagging product/solutions to coordinate.

maria: last check before handoff: 95p latency 980ms, error 0.8%, tpm down 61% for tempest. Leaving sculpt active. Handoff to @sam for night shift at 1967005278. :white_check_mark:

sam: ack. I'll monitor and escalate if we see >1.5s 95p or >1.5% errors. Saving commands to incident log.

incident-bot: Incident thread 1967004322 updated: mitigation applied, handoff scheduled to sam. Runbook attach: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/live-mitigation#tempest

maria: closing thread in 1h unless further updates. thanks everyone. :heart:
